components.purpose: The one place this product asks for authority to commit funds — and the only place it can be asked for.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centred column, space-y-4, p-6 — the consent skeleton /connect wears. h1, the explanation that connecting never asks for this, the permitted-operations list, the consequence block, the caps sentence, the grant form, and a visible way out.
constraints: This page must never be reachable as a side effect. The requirement forbids beginning a step-up on the product's own initiative, on a schedule, in response to a model, or as a side effect of reading anything — tests/agent/answer-authority.test.ts asserts that exactly one file in the whole product passes `stepUp: true`, and it is this page's server action.
`REQUESTED_SCOPES` must stay `['mcp:read']`; the step-up is a separate constant. tests/agent/wager.test.ts reads that constant out of the source and fails if the word 'wager' appears in it.

A personal deployment renders `<NothingToConnect>` — its scopes are an environment declaration this product cannot widen, and offering a button that cannot work is the failure 'A Remedy Named Must Exist In That Deployment' is about.
This surface asks for money authority, so it must not use urgency, scarcity or default-styling to encourage the grant. The way out is a peer of the grant, not a footnote.

components.purpose: Which operations the authority covers, in the words the operator reads.
components.current_implementation: A bulleted list rendered from STEP_UP_PERMITS — one source, so the surfaces naming these cannot drift. Names accepting as opening a position with the operator's money, and cancelling as committing nothing.
constraints: The wording comes from the domain constant and is never inlined here.

Both operations must stay named. Cancelling requires the same authority, and an operator who assumes otherwise will not understand the refusal they get — this is the surface where 'scope is not a safety boundary' becomes something a person has to act on.

components.purpose: The sentence being agreed to: this permits committing real money.
components.current_implementation: The consequence treatment every other confirmation in this product uses for the same job (DT-0005/DT-0007 role). States that the product will only spend on a trade the operator accepts themselves, that the authority is nonetheless real, and that it is theirs to withdraw at battlegrid.trade.
constraints: Must not be softened into reassurance. The requirement obliges the step-up to state that the authority permits committing the user's money, and the qualifier about how the product intends to use it does not replace that.
The withdrawal route must keep being named — it is the operator's only way back, and it is at BattleGrid rather than here.

components.purpose: Say that the platform's own limits continue to apply.
components.current_implementation: A text-sm secondary paragraph naming the three per-agent caps — what it may lose in a day, in total, and hold at once — and that BattleGrid enforces them whoever asks.
constraints: Required by the requirement's own wording ('the platform's own caps continue to apply'). This is spec-bearing copy, not reassurance, and must not be dropped as redundant.
It must not imply the caps make the authority safe — they bound the size of what can be spent, not whether it is spent.

actions.effect: Runs grantAnswerAuthority — the only caller in the product that requests fund-committing scope — and redirects to BattleGrid

components.current_implementation: A form with no hidden inputs and one `<PerformButton>` labelled 'Continue to BattleGrid to grant this'.
constraints: No hidden return address. The grant leaves through the OAuth callback, which knows nothing about this page, and tests/architecture/reachability.test.ts fails a control whose value no operation reads.

Nothing is recorded before BattleGrid answers — an abandoned step-up leaves no half-granted state and no authority the product claims but does not hold. A design must not add optimistic feedback implying otherwise.
Styling goes through BUTTON_PRIMARY in control.ts; 44px minimum tap target; focus ring is global.

actions.effect: Returns to the validated in-product path, or /approvals

components.current_implementation: A plain underlined link reading 'Not now — go back without granting anything'.
constraints: Must stay visible rather than implied. A page asking for authority over someone's money with no stated way out is a page that pressures.
The destination must remain an in-product path — the same validation the step-up link's `next` gets.

flows.name: Grant the authority
steps: arrive from a decision or the queue
read what it permits and that it commits real money
read that the platform caps still apply
return with the authority and answer the decision

flows.name: Decide not to
steps: back where you were, with nothing granted and nothing recorded

flows.name: Already granted
steps: told there is nothing to grant

flows.name: A configured deployment
steps: told there is nothing to connect — the scopes are an environment declaration
no button that could not work

accessibility.notes: No alerts on this surface — nothing has failed, and the page describes an intended state. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). The only client code is PerformButton.
